[STEP I 2004 Q6] The three points \(A,B,C\) have coordinates \(\left({p}_{1},{q}_{1}\right),\left({p}_{2},{q}_{2}\right)\) and \(\left({p}_{3},{q}_{3}\right)\), respectively. Verify that this point lies on the line joining \(C\) to the midpoint of \(AB\).\par The point \(H\) has coordinates \(\left({p}_{1}+{p}_{2}+{p}_{3},{q}_{1}+{q}_{2}+{q}_{3}\right)\). Show that if the line \(AH\) intersects the line \(BC\) at right angles, then \({p}_{2}^{2}+{q}_{2}^{2}={p}_{3}^{2}+{q}_{3}^{2}\), and write down a similar result if the line \(BH\) intersects the line \(AC\) at right angles.\par Deduce that if \(AH\) is perpendicular to \(BC\) and also \(BH\) is perpendicular to \(AC\), then \(CH\) is perpendicular to \(AB\).

\text{\[G=(\frac{p_1+p_2+p_3}{3},\frac{q_1+q_2+q_3}{3})\]G is two-thirds along each median. Writing position vectors A,B,C:\[(B+C)\cdot(C-B)=|C|^2-|B|^2=0\]Hence \(p_2^2+q_2^2=p_3^2+q_3^2\). Similarly BH perpendicular to AC gives \(p_1^2+q_1^2=p_3^2+q_3^2\). Thus\[(A+B)\cdot(B-A)=|B|^2-|A|^2=0\]and CH is perpendicular to AB.}
